# api_thinking
**Reads each third-party API's own model listing and syncs every model's real thinking levels into D
ads each third-party API's own model listing and syncs every model's real thinking levels into DSH**
中文 · MIT
> api_thinking is a community-maintained DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin. It is not a DeepSeek AI prod
i_thinking is a community-maintained DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin. It is not a DeepSeek AI product.
## The problem it solves
DSH's built-in model catalogue does not contain your third-party APIs. To get them into the model pi
cker at all, you declare an `llm-pi-ai` route by hand and list its `models:` yourself.
But **a hand-written `models:` list replaces the installed catalogue outright**. Those models are ne
ither in the catalogue nor declare `reasoningEfforts`, so `dsh-llm-pi-ai` treats them as non-reasoni
ng and **the composer offers no thinking levels**.
Writing the levels into YAML fixes that once — and goes stale immediately: nobody adds them when the
gateway ships a new model, and nobody updates them when upstream changes what it supports.
Yet an OpenAI-compatible gateway **usually already publishes that capability in its own model listin
g**. This plugin reads it and writes the result back into your configuration, so you stop maintainin
g that YAML by hand.
## Features
- **Automatic level sync** — requests each route's model listing and writes the levels the endpoint

publishes into the matching model's `reasoningEfforts`.
- **New APIs just work** — add a route, or a

dd models to an existing one; no plugin change, no restart.
- **Never invents capability** — an endp
oint that says nothing about reasoning is left exactly as it is; hand-written levels are never erase

d.
- **Owns exactly one field** — it owns `reasoningEfforts` and nothing else; comments, `!!js` expr

essions and every other field stay as they were.
- **Idempotent** — a sweep that finds nothing to ch

ange writes no file at all.
- **Self-diagnosing** — every load and every sweep records a status docu
ment, so there is always something to read when it misbehaves.
## Screenshots
*Once installed, the model picker offers the thinking levels a model actually supports.*
## Install
Requires a working DeepSeek Harness installation. The examples use the `desktop` profile — substitut
e your own profile name.
### From the plugin page
Open **Settings → Plugins** in the DSH web UI, search for `dsh-api-thinking` and install it. An agen
t can also call the plugin manager's `install_bundle` directly.
### From the command line

### Uninstall
Switch it off or uninstall it from the plugin page, or remove the `dsh-api-thinking` dependency from
that profile's `package.json` and delete it from the `dsh.profile.bundles` array.
## Usage
It works as soon as it is installed — **there is no switch to turn on**. The plugin walks every rout
e under the `llm-pi-ai` row:
| What you want | How |
| Get thinking levels on a model | Configure the route and its models in **Settings → Models** and g

ive it a moment |
| Add a new API | Add it in the model page; the levels follow on their own |
| Nar
row the scope | Set `routes` to the route names you care about; the default covers every OpenAI-comp

atible route |
| Change the sweep cadence | Set `intervalMs`; `0` means "sweep once after load, then

stop" |
| Find out why nothing happened | Read the status document — see Troubleshooting |
## Rules
A model's capability comes from the **first matching field** in the endpoint's model listing:
| Purpose | Fields, in priority order |

| Selectable levels | `reasoning_supported_efforts` → `supported_efforts` → `reasoning_efforts` |
|

Whether thinking can be turned off | `can_disable_thinking` → `reasoning_can_disable` |
| Whether it

reasons at all | `supports_reasoning` → `reasoning` |
| A pinned effort | `reasoning_effort` → `fix
ed_effort` → `effort` |
What gets written:
| The endpoint says | Written `reasoningEfforts` |
| A selectable set | `{ low: low, high: high, ... }`, filtered to the levels DSH can name (`off` / `

minimal` / `low` / `medium` / `high` / `xhigh` / `max`), in escalation order |
| No set, but one pin
ned effort | That single level — the picker shows what the model actually runs at (selecting it is a

no-op). Turn off with `fixedEffortAsLevel: false` |
| Explicit `supports_reasoning: false` | `false

n off with `fixedEffortAsLevel: false` |
| Explicit `supports_reasoning: false` | `false` |
[该节后续省略]
## Troubleshooting: why nothing happened
The host logger is not reliably reachable from a plugin, so every load and sweep writes its result t
o a status document (by default `$DSH_HOME/api-thinking.status.json`):
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Read these first:
| Field | Meaning |

| `phase` | Current stage (`apply` / `sweep`) |
| `error` | Failure reason, including request errors

the UI never shows |
| `listed` | How many models the endpoint returned |
| `models` | How many the

route has configured |
| `changes` | Which models this sweep planned to change |
| `wrote` / `via`
| Whether it wrote, and through which channel |
A non-empty `listed` with an empty `changes` usually means the endpoint publishes no reasoning capab
d` with an empty `changes` usually means the endpoint publishes no reasoning capability — see Rules.
## Known limitations
- It reads the **model listing** as its only source of capability. An endpoint that publishes nothin

g about reasoning is left alone.
- Only protocols that can list models are supported: `openai-comple

tions`, `openai-responses`, `anthropic-messages`.
- Models are matched by exact id; no aliases or fu

zzy matching.
- The default meaning of `off` is constrained by the pi-ai adapter, which cannot expre

ss "selectable but not the default".
- The fallback channel does no schema validation, only structur

al location.
- Writing `cordis.patch.yml` at the same time as the settings page can in theory overwr
ite each other; the next sweep converges again (it is idempotent).
